{{Short description|Russian astro- and plasma physicist (1936–2012)}}
{{Use British English|date=April 2026}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2026}}

'''Edward Mikhailovich Drobyshevski''' ({{langx|ru|Дробышевский, Эдуард Михайлович}}) (1936–2012), was a Russian astro- and plasma physicist.

==Career==
E.M. Drobyshevski was born in 1936. In 1959 he graduated the Leningrad Polytechnical Institute as an engineer-researcher. He was a Candidate of Physico-Mathematical sciences in 1965 and Doctor of Physico-Mathematical sciences in 1982. His scientific research career has been connected with the [[Ioffe Physico-Technical Institute]] of the Russian Academy of Sciences where his posts have been senior laboratory assistant (1959), junior scientist (1960), senior scientist (1979), leading scientist (1986), laboratory head (1991–2004), and major scientist (1993–2012).

==Contributions==
He has authored many theoretical and experimental studies on plasma physics, [[magnetohydrodynamics|MHD]], different branches of astrophysics (magnetic and [[binary stars]], [[Solar System]] evolution, origin of [[asteroids]] and [[comets]], [[astrobiology]], [[dark matter]], etc.), EM launch technology with industrial applications (for ~ 1&nbsp;g projectiles, world record velocities achieved), and the like.

He has put forward several novel and at times provocative scientific paradigms. The areas studied include:
* (1) generation of magnetic fields in celestial bodies by [[magnetohydrodynamics|MHD]] processes without positive feedback—"semi-dynamo";
* (2) close-binary [[Solar System]] cosmogony;
* (3) short-period [[comets]] and some other [[minor body|minor bodies]] as product of global explosions of [[electrolysis of water|electrolysed]] massive icy envelopes of distant moon-like bodies;
* (4) origin of life due to magneto-electrochemical processes in the Galilean satellites’ ensemble;
* (5) [[daemons in astrophysics|daemon]] paradigm considering the [[dark matter]] objects to be electrically charged (Ze ≈ 10e) elementary Planckian [[black hole]]s (m ≈ 2×10<sup>−5</sup>&nbsp;g, r<sub>g</sub> ≈ 3×10<sup>−33</sup>&nbsp;cm).

==Academic publications, membership of scientific societies and recognition==
He has more than 250 scientific publications, including about 120 in peer-reviewed journals, plus 3 inventions. He was a member of the Hypervelocity Impact Society and the [[European Astronomical Society]].

In 1992, the [[International Astronomical Union]] named the [[Themistian asteroid]] [[4009&nbsp;Drobyshevskij]] after him, in honour of his original [[cosmogonical]] ideas and theories of the origin of the planets and the minor bodies of the Solar System. It also noted that he was also known for his research on the magnetic fields of the sun and other stars.<ref>Schmadel, Lutz D. (2003) ''Dictionary of Minor Planet Names'', Springer p 342.</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=KWrB1jPCa8AC&pg=PA342&lpg=PA342&dq=4009+Drobyshevskij See also]</ref>

==Coverage in the media==
Some of his more controversial work has been noted in the popular press: His work on the [[Tunguska event]] has been noted in Popular Mechanics<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.popularmechanics.com/science/environment/natural-disasters/4316464|title = When Comets Attack: Solving the Mystery of the Biggest Natural Explosion in Modern History|date = 7 May 2009}}</ref> and Ria Novosti <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rian.ru/science/20090330/166427555.html|title = Ученый: тунгусская катастрофа связана с водородным взрывом ядра кометы|date = 30 March 2009}}</ref><ref>[https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=ru&u=http://www.rian.ru/science/20090330/166427555.html Ria Novosti: Scientist: Tunguska catastrophe associated with the explosion of a hydrogen nucleus of comet]</ref> as well as in The British Interplanetary Society's publication Spaceflight.<ref>http://www.bis-spaceflight.com/sitesia.aspx/page/183/id/2082/l/en{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> His work on ''Giant pieces of Jupiter's satellites'' as a threat to ''life on earth'' has been documented in [[Pravda]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pravda.ru/news/science/27-06-2008/273686-vzryv-0/|title=Гигантские осколки спутника Юпитера могут убить все живое на Земле|date=27 June 2008}}</ref>
